correctness.rationale: For each product support space \(V_{\mathbf L}\), ordinary duality gives \(\dim_Q(C\cap V_{\mathbf L})-\dim_Q(C^\perp\cap V_{\mathbf L^\perp})=k+\sum_i s_i-n\). The Gaussian binomial theorem turns the intersection dimensions into polynomial products, while blockwise orthogonal complementation bijects profiles. Double counting pairs of a dimension-\(r\) subcode and a containing support tuple proves the unitriangular inversion from Gaussian moments to exact support-profile counts. The proof covers zero-dimensional codes, zero-dimensional subcodes, and both signs of the shift. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks 25 product support spaces, nine profiles, subcode dimensions 0, 1, 2 and five shift values for an arbitrary non-MSRD code and its independently enumerated dual. The proof, not the finite test, establishes the universal statement.

value.rationale: The missing multiblock generalized weight duality is mathematically motivated by Molina (2026) Table 3; ordinary word enumerators and minimum generalized weights omit the exact support profile counts of higher-dimensional subcodes. The theorem supplies a full finite reversible all-rank transform for every linear code, with no MSRD or regularity assumption, and retains shot-wise support dimensions. This is a structural coding invariant with natural applications to multishot information exposure, not a tuned finite-slice computation or renaming. It does not assert a complexity bound or channel performance improvement.
